thread:
Oliver (Customer): hey team — hitting a weird one with EventSource in Safari (macOS + iOS). Stream starts then after ~7s the client shows open but no events. Reconnects sometimes never emit anything. Works fine in Chrome/FF.

Maya (Support): sorry you're seeing that, can you share repro steps and headers? is the API key in the query string or a header? any CDN in front? :thinking_face:

Oliver (Customer): quick repro: new EventSource('https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=redwood-mini&session=abc&api_key=TEST'); iOS 16 Safari. Sequence: initial connect -> we get a few events, then connection drops (network tab shows 200 -> subsequent reconnects show 304 if I reconnect quickly). If I open network tab and disable cache it works. no CORS errors in console.

Maya (Support): thanks. two quick suspects: 1) cached SSE response from the CDN returning 304 on conditional GETs, Safari handling of 304 + streamed responses is flaky; 2) API key in query string causing cache strat. Please don't include secrets in URLs — rotate that key after.

Nick (Support Bot): @Oliver — we created ticket #SUP-2026-179, attaching logs would help.

Oliver (Customer): attached a short HAR and these request/response snippets:

```
> GET /v1/streams?session=abc&api_key=TEST HTTP/1.1
> Accept: text/event-stream
> Host: api.redwood.example
> User-Agent: Safari/16
\n< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< Content-Type: text/event-stream
< Cache-Control: max-age=60, public
< ETag: "xyz"
< X-Edge-Cache: HIT
\n...event data (chunked)
\n--- later reconnect ---\n
> GET /v1/streams?session=abc&api_key=TEST HTTP/1.1
> If-None-Match: "xyz"
> Accept: text/event-stream
\n< HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified
< X-Edge-Cache: HIT
```

Maya (Support): that 304 is suspicious for SSE. many CDNs will return a 304 with no body and Safari's EventSource doesn't always reopen the stream body properly when the response is 304. If the edge serves a cached object for a streaming endpoint that should never be cached, you can get partial outputs or stuck connections.

Tony (Eng Runtime): pinging eng-runtime. @Sara fyi in case it's Fastly/CloudFront config. quick glance: our SSE endpoints are supposed to set `Cache-Control: no-store, no-transform` and `Vary: Accept`. if an old config leaked `public, max-age=60` that would explain it.

Sara (Eng Infra): looking at edge logs for the customer IP/time. I see the same ETag/304 pattern from the CDN. There's a VCL rule we added in 2024 that accidentally allowed `text/event-stream` through our caching layer in some POPs. Possible regression in the conditional GET handling.

Tony (Eng Runtime): thanks. short-term mitigation for customers: 1) move auth to Authorization header (Bearer token) not query string, 2) add a cache-buster param on connect e.g. `_ts=${Date.now()}` to force fresh GET, 3) for Safari specifically, client can detect stuck EventSource (no message for N seconds) and force a full reconnect using a different URL. longer-term: we should ensure edge never caches /v1/streams.

Maya (Support): sharing a suggested client polyfill workaround for Safari if you need one quickly: use fetch + ReadableStream to emulate SSE (works around Safari EventSource edge cases). example: 

```js
// lightweight fetch-based SSE reader
const res = await fetch('/v1/streams?model=redwood-mini', { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer <token>' } });
const reader = res.body.getReader();
const decoder = new TextDecoder();
let buf = '';
while (true) {
  const { value, done } = await reader.read();
  if (done) break;
  buf += decoder.decode(value, { stream: true });
  let lines = buf.split('\n\n');
  buf = lines.pop();
  for (const chunk of lines) {
    // parse SSE chunk, e.g. 'data: {"text":"hi"}'
    console.log('sse chunk', chunk);
  }
}
```

Oliver (Customer): can we get Redwood to change headers? I'm on hosted API. This is impacting production.

Sara (Eng Infra): escalation log: we changed the caching VCL on the POPs to bypass caching for `Accept: text/event-stream` and `path ~ "^/v1/streams"`. rolled to 3 POPs for canary. Patch includes: `set req.grace = 0; set req.http.Cache-Control = "no-store";` and remove `surrogate-control` for these routes. Deploy logs: `deploy-bot: release/edge-no-cache-streams -> canary`

deploy-bot: canary deploy started at 2026-03-15T14:12:00Z, roll percent 10%

Tony (Eng Runtime): added a server-side safety header to the stream response template: `Cache-Control: no-store, no-transform, must-revalidate`, `Vary: Accept, Authorization`, and `Surrogate-Control: no-store` + removed ETag generation for streaming routes. Putting note in change description to avoid adding ETag for streaming responses.

Maya (Support): @Oliver — patch is rolling. can you confirm after ~15 minutes if reconnects behave? Also please rotate the key you used in the URL (we flagged it).

Oliver (Customer): will do. quick Q: why does disabling cache in DevTools make it work?

Maya (Support): disabling cache forces a fresh GET with no If-None-Match header so CDN returns 200 with a live stream body. That's why it works.

Oliver (Customer): ok confirmed after ~20m — reconnects now consistently return 200 and the stream keeps delivering on Safari. thanks team. appreciate the quick turnaround. :raised_hands:

Tony (Eng Runtime): follow-ups: 1) we'll add an integration test against a Safari WebKit runner to hit streaming endpoints and assert no-cache headers. 2) docs PR to call out best practices (Authorization header, avoid query-string auth, cache rules).

Maya (Support): closing the support thread once we get your rotated token confirmation. leaving the ticket open for the infra postmortem and doc updates.

Oliver (Customer): rotated key and verified. you can close. cheers.
